chunks: And what Ṣafwān narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: Indeed, I perform Salat al-Layl, and I finish my prayer, and I perform the two rakʿahs; then I sleep for as long as Allah wills before dawn rises. Then if I awaken at dawn, I repeat them.

So the correct way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as referring to one who performs the two rakʿahs before the first dawn. It is recommended for him to repeat them so long as the second dawn has not yet risen, and that is not obligatory.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two recommended rakʿahs associated with fajr
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ الثَّانِي: the second or true dawn marking the entrance of fajr time
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ الْأَوَّلُ: the first dawn, before true dawn
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed before dawn

ai.seo_question: If the two rakʿahs of fajr are prayed before true dawn, should they be repeated?
ai.summary: This report discusses the timing of the two rakʿahs of fajr in relation to Salat al-Layl and dawn. It indicates that if they were performed before the first dawn, repeating them before the second dawn is recommended, not obligatory. The narration is therefore relevant to fiqh rulings on recommended prayers and their proper time.
